label: The v1 feature surface this repo uses classifies as 47 rows: 9 portable as-is, 21 with a mechanical change, 4 with a behavioural workaround, 9 irreducible, and 4 never established by this run. Every irreducible row is either an install-channel property or a v2 platform gap; none is a repo-code defect.

The two hardest compatibility gaps are not in the plugin API: reading message parts is blocked by v2's absent ctx.client plus a message list that carries no parts, and the global form of command.execute.before has no v2 hook at all. Both break plugins whose entire behaviour is side observation.

The single-file config promise is irreducible: v1 1.19.3 exits 1 with 'V2 permissions are not supported by OpenCode V1' rather than ignoring the key, so the only shared spelling is the v1 permission map, which caps what v2 can express because translation runs v1 to v2 and not back.

Mandating run --standalone buys per-child environment on v2 but costs all cross-client plugin state: on v2 plugins run inside a long-lived daemon shared by every concurrent client, while on v1 they run in a child of the CLI invocation, so counters, locks and caches held by system-deep-loop-guard and system-completion-sentinel must be persisted outside the process or keyed per session.

Three of the focus's named candidate gaps have zero evidence across iterations 1-19: the VS Code extension and CLAUDE.md appear nowhere, and LSP only as an unrelated v2 config-schema key and a v1 debug subcommand. The ledger marks them UNKNOWN with what would settle each rather than classifying them.

experimental.* splits into two classes rather than one: shell.env and chat.* have a destination in the migrate page, while experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.provider.small_model and experimental.text.complete are doc-stated irreducible. The repo uses none of the three today, so the cost is a ceiling on future v2 behaviour, not a present break.

Perfect compatibility for this repo means one plugin, agent, command and skill tree that loads and behaves on both versions with a named, documented capability delta; it cannot mean identical behaviour while nine rows are irreducible outside the repository.

direction: Repairing the (d) rows by editing repo code
reason: Each irreducible row is an install-channel property (upgrade --major, the missing v1 Homebrew formula) or a v2 platform gap (per-agent temperature, server-side toast, autocontinue, small_model, text.complete, global command observation), so no repository-side change reaches them; only documentation, detection and workarounds can.
